info.title: Cabros Bot API
info.description: Protected alerting and market-analysis APIs. Machine clients use the x-api-key header; the api-key query parameter is deprecated and exists only for legacy compatibility — it may leak through reverse-proxy access logs. A one-time per-process deprecation warning is emitted on use; setting API_KEY_QUERY_SUNSET (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) rejects query-parameter auth with 401 API_KEY_QUERY_REMOVED after the date. The browser admin console can use Firebase ID tokens on documented admin operations when ENABLE_FIREBASE_ADMIN_AUTH=true.

get.description: Returns a redacted, secrets-free snapshot of service name/version, uptime, enabled notification channels, and dependency readiness booleans. No API key required. Cached for 30 seconds per process. Returns 503 when the process is still bootstrapping or shutting down.

503.description: Service is not yet ready (bootstrap pending or shutdown draining)

get.description: Default behavior returns 200 with `uptime` JSON only. With `?deep=true`, the endpoint reuses the existing channel readiness logic from `/api/status` dependencies and returns 200 when every enabled channel is ready, 503 when any enabled channel is degraded. With `?depth=readiness`, it runs bounded external dependency probes (Firestore, Gemini, TradingView MCP, Binance, Telegram) and always returns 200 with the dependency report. The endpoint is never API-key protected.

parameters.name: deep
parameters.description: When `true`, include channel readiness and return 503 if any enabled channel is degraded.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Set to `readiness` to receive the external dependency validation report. This surface is advisory: it always returns HTTP 200 and reports degradation in the body's `ready` field, so a flaky third-party provider can never pull a healthy replica out of load-balancer rotation. Use `/ready?depth=dependencies` when you need a traffic-gating 503.

depthReadiness.summary: ?depth=readiness — always 200; degradation is reported in the body

503.description: Only `?deep=true` returns 503: one or more enabled notification channels are degraded, or readiness evaluation failed. The `?depth=readiness` variant never returns 503.

get.description: Two shapes, selected by `depth`. Without it, the bootstrap gate: 200 only after required startup components have completed bootstrap, 503 while pending or failed (`BootstrapReadiness`). With `?depth=dependencies`, the bootstrap verdict is ANDed with bounded external dependency probes for Firestore, Gemini, TradingView MCP, Binance, and Telegram, returning 503 when either the bootstrap is not ready or a considered dependency is unhealthy (`ReadinessReport`, which also echoes `status`, `components` and `bootstrapReady`). This endpoint checks neither continuous external provider health by default nor anything else implicitly. For an advisory, always-200 dependency report use `/healthcheck?depth=readiness`.

dependenciesHealthy.summary: /ready?depth=dependencies — bootstrap ready AND every considered dependency healthy

bootstrapReady.summary: Bare /ready — bootstrap gate only, no provider probes

503.description: At least one considered dependency is unhealthy (fail-closed variant only).

bootstrapPendingBlocksDependencies.summary: /ready?depth=dependencies — bootstrap still pending, so the gate stays 503 even though every dependency is healthy

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Set to `dependencies` to layer external provider probes on top of the bootstrap gate. This variant fails closed: it returns 503 when any considered dependency is unhealthy, so it is suitable as a load-balancer readiness gate.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency token (e.g. "3"). When present and not equal to the current preset version, the request returns 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED with the current preset so the client can rebase. When omitted, the write succeeds and increments version (backwards-compatible default). A malformed token (e.g. a comma-separated entity-tag list or the wildcard "*") returns 400 INVALID_IF_MATCH instead of being silently dropped.

post.summary: Preview a Binance Spot order without submitting it
post.description: Returns a BINANCE_ORDER_PREVIEW response with the LOT_SIZE-adjusted quantity, projected notional, estimated maker/taker fees, slippage estimate from a fail-open depth probe (4-second AbortController deadline), and a 5-second expiresAt token. The endpoint is read-only and never calls submitNewOrder. Preview-time validation reuses the same exchange-info filters and Binance order-test filters as POST /api/trading/binance/orders, but cannot be replayed after expiresAt. maxSlippageBps is honored for MARKET BUY orders that include a depth snapshot; wouldExceedBudget is reported when the slippageBps estimate exceeds the supplied budget but no order is rejected. BINANCE_TRADING_MAX_NOTIONAL is enforced — previews above the cap return 403 MAX_NOTIONAL_EXCEEDED.

post.summary: Validate or submit a Binance Spot order
post.description: Live requests require an idempotency key or clientOrderId. Decimal quantities, prices, and quote amounts may be strings to preserve precision. MARKET orders must omit timeInForce. Binance PERCENT_PRICE, PERCENT_PRICE_BY_SIDE, and account-dependent filters such as MAX_POSITION or MAX_NUM_ORDERS use Binance order-test validation before acceptance. Definitive pre-execution or exchange rejections return 400 BINANCE_ORDER_REJECTED; a reconciled order mismatch returns 409 BINANCE_ORDER_CONFLICT; transient order-test failures return retryable 502 BINANCE_VALIDATION_FAILED. Binance execution-unknown code -1006 remains BINANCE_ORDER_STATUS_UNKNOWN.

SummaryInterval.description: Optional bucket width for the summary.buckets time series (issue #1287). Omit it for the aggregate-only response, which is byte-for-byte unchanged. `hour` is capped at a 31-day window and `day` at 366 days; a wider window is rejected with 400 rather than silently narrowed. DeliveryMetrics.description: Aggregate in-memory delivery SLA counters exposed through /api/status and /api/capabilities. Reset on process restart. Omitted when no channel has recorded any delivery.

SignalClassClassification.description: In-memory counters for signal classification on the webhook ingest path. `featureFlags.signalClassMarker` only states that the badge marker is allowed to render; this block states whether alerts are actually being classified, so a silent regression back to 100% `unknown` is detectable instead of looking healthy. Counters reset on process restart, never block delivery or persistence, and the field is omitted entirely from /api/status when no alert has been classified yet. Contains only enum class names and counts — never alert text, symbols, or chat ids.

classifiedAlerts.description: Alerts that resolved to a class other than `unknown`.

byClass.description: Per-class counts keyed by the signalClass enum.

FirestoreWriteMetrics.description: In-memory counters for Firestore persistence attempts on alert storage, alert replays, and tradingviewJobs. Counters reset on process restart, never block delivery, and the field is omitted entirely from /api/status when nothing has been recorded yet. Mirrors DeliveryMetricsService for write-path observability so silent persistence failures cannot masquerade as 'Firestore ready'.

FirestoreReadMetrics.description: In-memory counters for Firestore read attempts. Added for issue #1285, where every stored-alert read endpoint answered 503 while writes succeeded and dependencies.firestore still reported ready: write success and credential shape could not detect a rejected query. readHealth is 'unknown' before any read is observed (no evidence, not a failure), 'healthy' after a successful read, and 'degraded' while the consecutive-failure streak is non-empty; only 'degraded' forces dependencies.firestore.ready to false. Counters reset on process restart and the field is omitted entirely when nothing has been recorded yet. The sanitized lastErrorCategory never carries the provider message, project path, or index definition.

FirestoreDependency.description: Firestore alert-storage dependency. enabled/configured reflect the ENABLE_FIRESTORE_ALERT_STORAGE gate and whether a usable credential was found; `configured` only validates credential shape. Since issue #1285 the verdict also reflects the observed read path: readHealth is 'unknown' until a read happens, 'healthy' after a successful read, and 'degraded' while the consecutive-failure streak is non-empty. A degraded read path forces ready:false and status:'degraded', so a deployment can no longer report a ready Firestore while every read endpoint answers 503 (issue #1285). The failure detail fields are present only while degraded.

FirestoreErrorCategory.description: Sanitized Firestore failure category. Never contains the provider message, credentials, project id, or index definition.

SelfTestResult.description: Self-test diagnostic suite result. Sensitive evidence is redacted server-side; secrets are never returned.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the size violation.

limit.description: Effective size limit (e.g., `256kb`) the request exceeded, parsed from WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_SIZE.

bySetupType.description: Per-setup-type breakdown mirroring the parent WindowStats shape. Each setup-type block is emitted only when at least one evaluated signal exists for that setup.

ShadowModeMetrics.description: Aggregated shadow-mode outcome metrics emitted by SignalOutcomeService.getMetricsSummary(). The object form is returned only when totalSignalsReceived > 0 and signal-outcome tracking is enabled. When the service has no data or tracking is disabled, the field becomes the string sentinel "No measurements found". Win-rate semantics (see issue GH-593): hitRatePercent counts evaluated window outcomes whose return > 0; targetHitRatePercent/stopHitRatePercent count explicit target/stop hits including firstHit fallbacks and use barrier-eligible denominators (evaluated outcomes without a configured target or stop are excluded instead of counted as misses); expectancyR averages rMultiple over evaluated windows with finite rMultiple. All rates use evaluated-window denominators and zero-fill when none are eligible.

StoredAlert.description: Stored alert document. The `source` field identifies the producing flow (webhook, news-monitor, market-scanner, expanded-analysis, test-alert). When the report text exceeded the 20,000-character storage cap, `truncated: true` and `originalLength` are populated so consumers and replay can flag the loss; replay will redeliver only the truncated text.

enrichmentData.description: Persisted enrichment payload. Unlike the dry-run response, this is the document written by `AlertStorageService.saveAlert()`, so it additionally carries the GH-599 computed-provenance fields that are only added at persist time.

current_price.description: Persisted entry-price context. Sourced from TradingView MCP when tradingViewEnrichmentApplied is true, from the alert-enrichment model response over grounded context when only Gemini enrichment ran, or from a derived quote when neither provider supplied a usable price (GH-599). Omitted entirely when no provider returned a finite positive price. Note: this is the model's reading of grounded context, not a snippet-level price extraction, so it carries no field-level citation.

price_currency.description: Uppercased ISO-4217-style currency code declared by the provider alongside current_price (e.g. "USD", "USDT"). Omitted when current_price is absent, when the derived-quote fallback supplied the price, or when the code fails the 2-5 uppercase-letter validation (GH-599).

risk_reward_ratio_source.description: Set to 'computed' on the stored document when risk_reward_ratio was deterministically derived at persist time from current_price / invalidation_level / target_level / side, because the provider omitted it or reported a non-positive value that could not be used. Absent (or null) when the value came from the LLM or MCP provider, or when the deterministic computation could not run (GH-599). This field exists only on the persisted document: the dry-run response returns before `applyDeterministicRiskReward()` runs, so a dry-run payload never carries it.

levelsSource.description: Provenance of the emitted risk levels. 'tradingview-mcp' when the MCP ATR-derived block won (the default for MCP-sourced alerts); 'gemini-grounding' when Gemini-parsed levels were emitted because TradingView MCP data was absent or failed (GH-509 / CB-226); 'fallback-trade-plan' when MCP supplied the price but its ATR-derived block was rejected as zero, non-finite, or failing the side/positivity checks and the secondary heuristic timeframe risk plan was used instead (GH-1229); 'derived-quote' when levels were derived from a fetched quote because neither provider returned a usable block (GH-599).

priceSource.description: Provider that supplied the emitted current_price. 'tradingview-mcp' from the MCP quote, 'gemini-grounding' from the alert-enrichment model response over grounded context, 'derived-quote' from a fetched quote fallback. When a risk block was completed arithmetically because it supplied both directional levels but no ratio, the emitted entry is the one that ratio was derived from, so current_price is reported as 'gemini-grounding' and price_currency is omitted: a quote currency describing a different price must not be attached to this one. This keeps (current_price, invalidation_level, target_level, risk_reward_ratio) internally consistent, so the stored ratio can always be recomputed from the stored fields (GH-599).

signalClass.description: Classification category for the alert signal.

truncated.description: True when the stored text was clipped to the 20,000-character cap; see originalLength for the pre-truncation size.

originalLength.description: Length of the original alert text in characters before the 20,000-character cap was applied.

currentPrice.description: Top-level mirror of enrichmentData.current_price when present and finite positive (GH-599 / CB-XXX). Sourced from Gemini grounding snippets when only the alert-enrichment prompt ran, and from TradingView MCP when tradingViewEnrichmentApplied is true.

priceCurrency.description: Top-level mirror of enrichmentData.price_currency when currentPrice is present (GH-599 / CB-XXX).

ReplayAttempt.description: Audit record for a single replay attempt. Each call to POST /api/alerts/{alertId}/replay creates a unique document so repeated replays with the same idempotency key do not overwrite prior attempts; the HTTP Idempotency-Replay contract is preserved upstream by the idempotency middleware. Raw idempotency keys are never persisted; only a SHA-256 hash prefix is exposed so attempts can be grouped without leaking the caller-supplied key.

id.description: Opaque replay-attempt identifier; use this value for display and audit references, not as the Firestore document ID.

idempotencyKeyHashPrefix.description: First 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 hash of the supplied idempotency key. The raw key is never stored or returned.

window.description: The effective window the aggregates were computed over. Contains from, to, limit and maxDays. When the interval parameter is supplied it also contains interval, and maxDays reports that interval's cap (31 for hour, 366 for day) instead of the aggregate-only 31.

buckets.description: Present only when the interval parameter is supplied (issue #1287). Time-bucketed alert volume and delivery outcomes, ascending by bucketStart, with empty buckets zero-filled so a chart has no gaps and the array length is predictable for a given window and interval. Derived from the same limit-bounded sample as the aggregates, so sum(bucket.total) equals totalAlerts.

byFeatureFlag.description: Includes tradingViewData for requested MCP enrichment, tradingViewDataApplied for successfully applied MCP results, and withoutTradingViewData for requests that did not opt in.

costByFeature.description: Token usage and cost attribution by feature. Records are attributed from their persisted tokenUsage.byFeature tags; legacy records without tags fall back to their alert source, and records with no real token usage are not attributed at all. totalCost is an estimate from published list pricing (unrecognized models use the default rate, never 0); alerts counts stored documents, batches counts distinct news-monitor requests grouped by requestId/batchId, and symbols counts distinct symbols across a batch including multi-symbol reports stored as a single document.

signalClassCounts.description: Aggregate count of stored alerts per signal class (breakout, mean_reversion, trend_continuation, reversal, volume_spike, news_event, manual, unknown).

tradingViewStatusCounts.description: Counts TradingView enrichment outcomes; requested alerts without a stored status are reported as unrecorded.

evidenceCoverage.description: Tracks whether enriched alerts cited grounding sources. Denominator counts only enriched alerts; legacy records missing a sources field count as zero. Grouped by prompt provenance (Langfuse vs. local fallback) for regression attribution.

denominator.description: Number of enriched alerts included in this coverage window.

totalSourceCount.description: Sum of all source counts across enriched alerts in the window.

averageSourceCount.description: Average number of cited sources per enriched alert. 0 when denominator is 0.

byPromptProvenance.description: Per-provenance breakdown (Langfuse version, local fallback, etc.) using the same bucket shape.

shadowModeMetrics.description: Aggregated shadow-mode outcome metrics. When an object, includes the full OutcomesSummary payload (coverage buckets, per-window WindowStats with hit/target/stop rates and expectancyR, drawdown proxy, latency/cost metadata, and falsePositiveCandidates). When no data is available or signal-outcome tracking is disabled, the value is the string sentinel "No measurements found". Equity providers remain opt-in and fail open. This field is omitted when source or enriched filters are supplied because shadow-mode metrics do not support those filters. Win-rate field semantics: hitRatePercent counts evaluated window outcomes whose return > 0; targetHitRatePercent/stopHitRatePercent count explicit target/stop hits (including firstHit fallbacks) over barrier-eligible denominators only; expectancyR averages finite rMultiple over evaluated windows.

SentimentCalibration.description: Distribution of stored enriched-alert sentiment_score magnitudes in the summary window, used to detect a saturated score that can no longer rank alerts (GH-1031). Scores are read as absolute magnitudes, so a BEARISH score contributes its positive magnitude. Denominator counts only enriched alerts that stored a usable score.

sampleCount.description: Enriched alerts in the window that stored a usable sentiment_score.

evaluated.description: True only when sampleCount reached the sample floor. False means saturation is deliberately not declared because there is too little evidence.

saturated.description: True when the distribution is judged unusable for ranking.

reason.description: Which rule produced the verdict. null means healthy. spread_collapse is p90 - p10 below the spread floor; top_band_concentration is at least 75% of samples at or above 0.75; insufficient_sample and no_samples mean no verdict was reached.

min.description: Lowest magnitude in the window, or null when there are no samples.

max.description: Highest magnitude in the window, or null when there are no samples.

spread.description: p90 - p10. Compared against the spread floor to detect a collapsed distribution.

distinctValueCount.description: Number of distinct magnitudes observed. Diagnostic only, never a saturation trigger, because anchoring the prompt to score bands intentionally concentrates output onto band centres.

bucketCount.description: Number of non-empty 0.1-wide buckets. Diagnostic only; a post-anchor rollout is expected to occupy at least 4.

buckets.description: Histogram of magnitudes in 0.1-wide bands, ascending. Only non-empty bands are listed.

topBandCount.description: Samples at or above the top-band floor (0.75).

topBandShare.description: topBandCount divided by sampleCount, or null when there are no samples.

rawScoreCapCount.description: Alerts in the window that also stored sentiment_score_raw, meaning the zero-source cap (CB-238) rewrote their score. A non-zero value proves the cap is live in this deployment.

IdempotencyStorage.description: Durable webhook idempotency state. Every Firestore error in this layer is swallowed so the request falls back to in-memory idempotency, which is why `ready` is proven from observed durable work rather than inferred from credential shape: a deployment whose credentials look valid but cannot reach Firestore reports `degraded`, and a process that has not yet attempted a durable operation reports `unverified`.

enabled.description: ENABLE_FIRESTORE_IDEMPOTENCY (or the deprecated ENABLE_FIRESTORE_IDEMPOTENCY_STORAGE alias) is true.

configured.description: Firestore credential shape only. True does not mean durability works.

ready.description: True only after an observed successful durable operation, and false again from the first failure until the next success. It never implies `configured`.

status.description: `unverified` is no evidence, not health: it is the normal state right after a restart until the first keyed request is served. Gate state wins over observed provider health.

mode.description: Configured intent: durable means Firestore is the target and ephemeral means the feature is off or unconfigured. Read `ready`/`status` for whether durability is actually in effect.

failOpen.description: Always true. Firestore failures degrade to in-memory idempotency rather than failing the request, so a `degraded` verdict still delivers alerts; it just cannot suppress a duplicate after a restart or across replicas.

collection.description: Firestore collection holding hashed idempotency reservations. Raw caller keys are never stored as document ids or logged.

operationsAttempted.description: Durable use attempts, including attempts whose Firebase initialization was rejected. Never incremented by a status read.

consecutiveFailures.description: Cleared by the next success, so a transient outage self-heals without a restart.

lastErrorReason.description: Closed enum so a Firestore error message — which embeds the project and database path — can never reach a status response.

NewsAnalysisStorage.description: Durable news-monitor analysis records (issue #1180). Every Firestore error in this service is swallowed so news alert delivery is never blocked, which is why `ready` is proven from observed durable work rather than inferred from credential shape: a deployment whose credentials look valid but cannot reach Firestore reports `degraded`, and a process that has not yet recorded or read an analysis reports `unverified`. Counters are process-local and reset on restart, so `unverified` is the normal state right after every deploy.

enabled.description: ENABLE_FIRESTORE_NEWS_ANALYSIS is true. Environment-only: it is deliberately absent from the Remote Config allow-list because a published template parameter's defaultValue is reported with source `remote` and would override this env var.

configured.description: Firestore credential shape only. True does not mean persistence works.

ready.description: True only after an observed successful durable write or read, and false again from the first failure until the next success.

status.description: `unverified` is no evidence, not health. Gate state wins over observed provider health.

mode.description: Configured intent. It stays `durable` while the gate is on even after a failure, because `memory` would read as the flag being off.

failOpen.description: Always true. Firestore failures degrade to unrecorded analysis rather than failing the news monitor, so a `degraded` verdict still delivers alerts; it just stops recording an audit trail.

collection.description: Firestore collection holding persisted news analysis records.

retentionDays.description: Effective NEWS_ANALYSIS_RETENTION_DAYS (1-365, default 30), applied as the document `expiresAt` field. Honoured only once the project's Firestore TTL policy exists.

operationsAttempted.description: Durable use attempts, including attempts whose Firebase initialization was rejected. Never incremented by a status read.

consecutiveFailures.description: Cleared by the next success, so a transient outage self-heals without a restart.

lastErrorReason.description: Closed enum so a Firestore error message — which embeds the fully-qualified project/database path — can never reach a status response.

lastMissingIndex.description: True when the most recent failure was a rejected query caused by an undeployed composite index. `news_analysis` reads filter on symbol/eventCategory and sort on createdAt, and Firestore does not merge single-field indexes, so the composites declared in firestore.indexes.json must be deployed with `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`.

LangfusePromptDependency.description: Langfuse dynamic prompt management. `configured` is credential shape only: a typo'd, revoked or wrong-project key satisfies it and can still resolve zero prompts. `PromptService` fails open to the local file on any remote failure, so before this contract a deployment that fell back on every alert reported the same `ready` verdict as a working one and the enablement was unverifiable. `ready` is therefore proven from observed resolutions. This is the fifth instance of the repository's 'shape is not readiness' rule, after `firebaseRemoteConfig.ready` (#598), Firestore `readHealth` (#1285), `equityMarketData.ready` (#1116) and `idempotencyStorage.ready` (#1111).

configured.description: Both LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY are non-empty. Credential shape only; never implies a prompt can be fetched.

ready.description: True only after an observed successful prompt resolution, and false again from the first failure until the next success. Never implies `configured`.

status.description: `unverified` is no evidence, not health. Gate state wins over observed provider health.

failOpen.description: Always true. A remote failure falls back to the local prompt file, so a `degraded` verdict still enriches and delivers alerts; it just means the managed prompt version was not the one used.

baseUrlHost.description: Host of LANGFUSE_BASE_URL. Only the host is reported, because a base URL can carry an embedded credential or path token.

label.description: Configured LANGFUSE_PROMPT_LABEL, or null when the code default applies (`production` in production-like environments, `latest` elsewhere).

cacheTtlSeconds.description: Effective LANGFUSE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS passed to the Langfuse SDK prompt cache, or null when unparseable.

promptsAttempted.description: Remote prompt resolutions attempted, including attempts whose client initialization was refused. Never incremented by a status read.

localFallbackCount.description: Resolutions that fell back to the local prompt file while the gate was on. Always 0 while the gate is off, where local use is the configured intent rather than a fallback.

consecutiveFailures.description: Cleared by the next success, so a transient outage self-heals without a restart and the verdict never latches degraded.

lastErrorReason.description: Closed enum. A Langfuse error body can embed the project id, base URL and API key, so an unrecognized failure collapses to `langfuse_unavailable` and raw provider text never reaches this response. `langfuse_prompt_not_found` is the signature of a label that was never published.

byPrompt.description: Per-prompt resolution provenance, so a partial rollout is visible: how many resolved from Langfuse, how many fell back locally, how many failed, and the last label/version seen. Process-local and bounded.

localFallbackByPrompt.description: Prompts currently falling back to the local file, with counts. Empty when every registered prompt resolved from Langfuse.

schemaDrift.description: Present only when the gate is on and at least one managed prompt has been observed. A Langfuse prompt that has not been republished after a local-fallback contract change (for example #1031) is reported here rather than as a failure: it means the managed prompt is behind the code, and the missing markers are listed.

SignalOutcomeWorker.description: Signal outcome evaluation worker state. The evaluation sweep is claimed with a Firestore lease in `signalOutcomeLocks` so exactly one process prices a pending signal when more than one has tracking enabled, which is the production topology (`render.yaml` declares a web-role process and the dedicated `cabros-crypto-bot-signal-outcome-worker`). The lease observability fields identify the winning evaluator from status alone instead of inferring it from the Render dashboard. Lease failures are fail-open: a lease write that cannot be attempted does not stop evaluation.

configured.description: Firestore credential shape only. True does not mean outcome evaluation can reach its collection.

role.description: Which entrypoint this process is permitted to start the sweep from. Role gating alone does not stop two enabled replicas from sweeping; the lease does.

batchLimit.description: SIGNAL_OUTCOME_EVALUATION_BATCH_LIMIT pending signals scanned per sweep.

maxDurationMs.description: SIGNAL_OUTCOME_EVALUATION_MAX_DURATION_MS sweep duration budget. Independently tunable from the lease, so a lease shorter than this budget can be taken over mid-sweep.

leaseMs.description: Effective distributed sweep lease duration in milliseconds. SIGNAL_OUTCOME_EVALUATION_LEASE_MS, default 120000, valid range 10000-600000, environment-only. Values outside the range fall back to the default.

lastRunLeaseHeld.description: The most recent sweep did not run to completion as the lease holder, either because another replica held the lease at claim time or because ownership was lost mid-sweep. A sweep aborted by a lost lease can still report a non-zero lastRunEvaluatedCount for the documents it finished before losing ownership.

leaseHeldSkipCount.description: Cumulative sweeps since process start that did not run to completion as the lease holder. One replica whose counter climbs while its lastRunEvaluatedCount stays at zero is not the evaluator.

lastRunAt.description: A lastRunAt that never advances means the sweep is not running, whatever featureFlags.signalOutcomeTracking reports.

entryPriceSources.description: Effective non-secret crypto and equity entry-price provider chains.

ScannerPresetStorage.description: Scanner-preset persistence state. `mode` and `backend` are intent-derived: they report the configured target and must not flip to `memory` while ENABLE_FIRESTORE_SCANNER_PRESETS=true and credentials are present, because an operator reading `memory` concludes the feature is off. `status` separates the three causes that need different action — `disabled` (ENABLE_FIRESTORE_SCANNER_PRESETS is not true), `misconfigured` (credentials genuinely absent or rejected), and `degraded` (a durable operation failed and nothing has answered since). `unverified` means no durable operation has been observed yet: neither healthy nor broken, and the normal state immediately after a restart.

configured.description: Whether Firestore credentials are present and a client can be constructed. This is credential shape only and must not be read as proof that presets persist; read `ready`/`status` instead.

ready.description: True only when status is `ready`, i.e. a durable scanner-preset read or write has actually succeeded. GET /api/status proves this with a bounded durable read, so no prior write is required.

mode.description: Intent-derived: `durable` means the service is configured to use Firestore and will keep doing so across a restart. `ephemeral` is reported only when the gate is off or credentials are unusable, in which case presets may be lost on restart.

backend.description: Intent-derived counterpart of `mode`. A `degraded` store still reports `firestore`, because presets are still being written to Firestore and local records are retried.

failOpen.description: Always true. Preset CRUD keeps serving from the in-memory mirror when Firestore is unavailable, so a degraded verdict does not mean the endpoint fails.

readiness.description: Observed-window verdict behind `status`: `degraded` when the most recent durable operation failed, `verified` when one has succeeded, `unverified` when none has been observed.

collection.description: Firestore collection backing durable scanner presets.

operationsAttempted.description: Durable reads and writes observed in this process. Counted even when Firebase initialization is rejected, because asking for durable storage and not getting it is the event an operator needs to see.

consecutiveFailures.description: Failures since the last success. A transient error therefore downgrades the verdict only until the next success, with no restart required to recover.

lastErrorReason.description: Closed sanitized failure class. Never a provider message: a Firestore error embeds the fully-qualified project/database path.

pendingWrites.description: Local records still awaiting a successful durable write. Reported separately from the verdict because an unsynced record is a pending-sync fact, not a store fault, and must never flip `mode`/`backend`.

pendingDeletes.description: Local deletion tombstones still awaiting a successful durable delete.

oldestPendingWriteAt.description: Updated timestamp of the oldest unsynced local write, or null when there is none. Shows how long a record has been stuck.

lastReadFellBack.description: True when the most recent durable read or write failed. Cleared by the next success.

SymbolAnalysisStorage.description: Durable symbol-analysis history behind `/api/symbol-analyses`. Every Firestore error in this layer is swallowed into a dropped record so a symbol analysis never fails, which is why `ready` is proven from an observed successful **write** rather than inferred from credential shape: a deployment whose credentials look valid but cannot reach Firestore reports `degraded`. A successful read only proves Firestore reachability, never that analyses are being stored, so read counters are reported separately and do not flip the verdict.

enabled.description: ENABLE_SYMBOL_ANALYSIS_STORAGE is true. Environment-only: excluded from Remote Config so a published server template cannot override render.yaml. This is configured intent, not evidence that persistence works.

configured.description: Firestore credential shape only. True does not mean the collection is reachable or writable.

ready.description: True only after an observed successful durable write, and false again from the first failure until the next success. It never implies `configured`, and reading the collection does not set it.

status.description: `unverified` is no evidence, not health: it is the normal state right after a redeploy until the first analysis is persisted. Gate state wins over observed provider health.

failOpen.description: Always true. A Firestore failure drops the record and still answers the symbol analysis, so a `degraded` verdict means decision history silently stops accumulating rather than that analysis is unavailable.

collection.description: Firestore collection group backing the history.

retentionDays.description: Days before a document expires. `expiresAt` is only honoured once the Firestore TTL policy exists (`bash ops/configure-operational-collection-retention.sh`); until then the collection grows without bound.

writesAttempted.description: Durable write attempts, including those where Firebase initialization was rejected — asking for durable storage and not getting it is the event an operator needs to see. A rejected initialization is charged to the operation that triggered it, so browsing the collection never increments this counter.

readsAttempted.description: Durable read attempts, including those where Firebase initialization was rejected. Attribution follows the triggering operation, so a read that fails to initialize is counted here and never as a write.

readsSucceeded.description: Proves Firestore reachability only. A non-zero value does not mean analyses are being persisted.

consecutiveFailures.description: Clears on the next successful Firestore operation, so a transient outage self-heals without a restart and never latches degraded.

lastErrorReason.description: Closed enum so a Firestore error message — which embeds the fully-qualified project and database path — can never leak into a status response.

telegramChatId.description: Optional Telegram chat ID override. When ENABLE_STRICT_CHAT_ID_VALIDATION=true, must match a numeric chat ID (5-20 digits, optional '-' prefix); free-form strings are rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST.

telegramThreadId.description: Optional Telegram forum topic message_thread_id override (0 routes to the chat general topic).

whatsappChatId.description: Optional WhatsApp chat ID override. When ENABLE_STRICT_CHAT_ID_VALIDATION=true, must match the GreenAPI format <digits>@<c.us|g.us>; free-form strings are rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST.

lockedUntil.description: When the preset is held by an in-flight sweep. Updates return 409 PRESET_LOCKED while this timestamp is in the future.

version.description: Monotonic per-preset version used for optimistic concurrency. Increment by 1 on every successful update. Echoed as the ETag response header and accepted via the If-Match request header on PUT/DELETE.

ScannerPresetConflictResponse.description: Conflict response for scanner-preset If-Match / lockedUntil failures. Returned with HTTP 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED and HTTP 409 PRESET_LOCKED so the client can rebase or wait for the scheduler lease to release.

error.description: Human-readable explanation of why the request was rejected.

preset.description: Current preset state, including its monotonic version, so the client can rebase.

lockedUntil.description: Echoed on 409 PRESET_LOCKED responses so the client knows when the scheduler lease expires.

CallbackFields.description: When callbackUrl is configured, each callback POST includes x-callback-timestamp (ISO-8601), x-callback-event, and a UUID x-callback-delivery-id. If a callback secret is configured (via callbackSecret or JOB_CALLBACK_SIGNING_SECRET), x-callback-signature is sent containing an HMAC-SHA256 hex digest over the newline-delimited timestamp, event, delivery ID, and raw JSON body. The secret itself is never transmitted. Hostname callback delivery is pinned to the public DNS answers that passed private-address validation for that attempt, preventing a second lookup from selecting a private destination; ALLOW_PRIVATE_CALLBACKS=true is an explicit override. Receivers should reject stale timestamps and deduplicate delivery IDs; retries use new IDs and signatures.

callbackUrl.description: HTTPS URL to receive a POST with the job result when it reaches a terminal state (or a configured intermediate event). HTTP is allowed only for localhost in development. Hostname callback connections are pinned to the validated public DNS answers for each attempt; any private DNS answer is rejected unless ALLOW_PRIVATE_CALLBACKS=true.

callbackSecret.description: Optional shared secret used to generate the x-callback-signature HMAC-SHA256 header. The secret is used server-side to compute the signature and is never transmitted in callback requests.

callbackEvents.description: Events that trigger a callback delivery. Defaults to all terminal events: completed, failed, cancelled, timed_out.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum runtime for the job in milliseconds. Defaults to 300000 (5 minutes). Hard cap at 600000 (10 minutes).

dryRun.description: When true, analyze without notification delivery or persistence. The query parameter form is supported for GET and POST.

telegramChatId.description: Optional Telegram chat ID override. When ENABLE_STRICT_CHAT_ID_VALIDATION=true, must match a numeric chat ID (5-20 digits, optional '-' prefix); free-form strings are rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST.

telegramThreadId.description: Optional Telegram forum topic message_thread_id override (0 routes to the chat general topic).

whatsappChatId.description: Optional WhatsApp chat ID override. When ENABLE_STRICT_CHAT_ID_VALIDATION=true, must match the GreenAPI format <digits>@<c.us|g.us>; free-form strings are rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST.

dryRun.description: Present and true when analysis generated alerts without dispatching or persisting them.

quota_exhausted.description: Number of symbols that exhausted Gemini 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED retries.

throttled.description: Number of alert candidates throttled due to global batch or window volume caps.

requestedChannels.description: Channels selected for delivery; in dry-run mode these are intended channels.

deliveredChannels.description: Channels that actually received alerts; empty in dry-run mode.

alertsDelivered.description: Number of alerts delivered in the current sliding window.

alertsThrottled.description: Number of alerts throttled in the current sliding window.

windowResetsAt.description: Timestamp when the current sliding window resets.

NewsMonitorResult.description: Per-symbol news-monitor analysis result. The optional `alert` object carries the risk-barrier fields (`stop`, `target`) whenever a finite, on-side-of-entry barrier is available from market context or `deriveBarriers()`.

NewsGroundingCalibration.description: Grounding-derived source metadata used to calibrate the news-monitor confidence score. `qualityTier` and `qualityPenalty` were added in issue #1230 and are always present; `qualityTier` is `null` and `qualityPenalty` is `1` when no tier was resolved (no grounding sources, or grounding derivation failed).

grounding_used.description: True when the actual grounding search results were available to derive source metadata from.

model_source_count.description: Source count as emitted by the model, before grounding override.

model_source_freshness.description: Source freshness score as emitted by the model, before grounding override.

model_source_quality.description: Source quality score as emitted by the model, before grounding override.

effective_source_count.description: Source count actually used for the source-count penalty.

effective_source_freshness.description: Freshness score actually used for the freshness penalty.

effective_source_quality.description: Quality score actually used for the source-authority penalty.

freshness_unknown.description: True when grounding sources carried no explicit dates, so a conservative unknown-freshness penalty was applied.

qualityTier.description: Weakest (most penalty-bearing) domain-quality tier present in the grounding sources. `null` when no tier was resolved.

qualityPenalty.description: Bounded multiplicative penalty applied to the additive-penalty-adjusted confidence. Always <= 1, so the quality step can only reduce a score. `1` means no penalty was applied.

actual_source_count.description: Number of grounding search results returned.

actual_source_quality.description: Average domain-quality score across the grounding sources (0..1).

actual_source_freshness.description: Average freshness score across the dated grounding sources (0..1).

actual_quality_tiers.description: Per-tier counts across the grounding sources.

actual_source_domains.description: Normalized hostnames classified from the grounding sources.

actual_stale_sources.description: Grounding sources older than the freshness window.

actual_dated_sources.description: Grounding sources that carried an explicit date.

has_explicit_dates.description: True when at least one grounding source carried an explicit date.

actual_freshness_reason.description: Human-readable freshness classification used for the penalty decision.

NewsAlert.description: Structured news alert payload returned by `/api/news-monitor`. Optional numeric `stop` and `target` risk barriers are present whenever a finite, on-side-of-entry value is available from market context or `deriveBarriers()`; otherwise they are omitted.

sourceQualityTier.description: Weakest domain-quality tier resolved from the grounding sources (issue #1230). Present only when grounding returned at least one source. The tier drives a bounded multiplicative confidence penalty (`high` x1, `medium` x0.95, `low` x0.85, `unknown` x1). `unknown` is reported for auditing but applies no penalty: it means the domain is not in the classification lists, which cover only ~56 domains, so penalizing it would reduce confidence whenever a reputable outlet is added to an otherwise well-sourced set. The penalty is applied after the additive source-count, freshness, and authority penalties. Omitted when no tier was resolved (no grounding, or zero grounding sources), in which case no quality penalty is applied.

stop.description: Optional numeric stop barrier in the same units as `marketContext.price`. Populated when market context supplies a stop or `deriveBarriers()` produces a finite, on-side-of-entry value; omitted otherwise.

target.description: Optional numeric target barrier in the same units as `marketContext.price`. Populated when market context supplies a target or `deriveBarriers()` produces a finite, on-side-of-entry value; omitted otherwise.

suppressedRepeat.description: True when this alert was persisted without channel delivery because it repeated a recent signal.

requestId.description: Request correlation ID echoed from the inbound x-request-id header or generated as a UUIDv4.

signalClass.description: Classification category for the alert signal.

tradingViewEnrichmentApplied.description: True only when TradingView MCP data was successfully applied to this enrichment.

tradingViewEnrichmentStatus.description: Sanitized TradingView MCP outcome for this alert.

exchange.description: Exchange prefix reported by the upstream screener, unchanged by outbound MCP venue aliasing (GH-591).

requestedExchange.description: Exchange prefix that was requested by the screener for the outbound TradingView MCP call. Alias resolution never rewrites this value (GH-591).

requestedExchangeMappedTo.description: Venue the outbound TradingView MCP call was actually sent to when the screener's exchange prefix had no equivalent venue on the MCP server (for example 'BATS' -> 'NASDAQ'). Omitted when no alias was applied (GH-591).

levelsSource.description: Provenance of the emitted risk levels (invalidation_level / target_level / risk_reward_ratio). 'tradingview-mcp' when the MCP ATR-derived block won, which is the default for MCP-sourced alerts. 'gemini-grounding' only when Gemini-parsed fallback levels are emitted because TradingView MCP data was absent or failed (GH-509 / CB-226). 'fallback-trade-plan' when TradingView MCP supplied the price but its ATR-derived risk block was rejected (zero, non-finite, or failing the side/positivity checks) and the secondary heuristic timeframe risk plan was used instead (GH-1229). 'derived-quote' when levels were derived from the MCP quote because neither provider returned a usable block (GH-599).

current_price.description: Current entry-price context. Sourced from TradingView MCP when tradingViewEnrichmentApplied is true; sourced from Gemini grounding snippets (alert-enrichment prompt response) when only Gemini enrichment ran (GH-599 / CB-XXX). Null when neither provider supplies a finite positive price.

price_currency.description: ISO-4217-style currency code paired with current_price when supplied by Gemini grounding (e.g. "USD", "USDT"); null when current_price is absent or currency is not declared (GH-599 / CB-XXX).

sentiment_score.description: Signed sentiment magnitude, negative for bearish and positive for bullish. NEUTRAL alerts always carry 0. The prompt scores this against fixed reference anchors (0.90 / 0.75 / 0.60 / 0.45 / 0.30, GH-1031) so the value separates strong setups from weak ones; it is clamped to the zero-source cap of 0.55 when grounding returned no sources, with the pre-cap value preserved in sentiment_score_raw.

sentiment_score_raw.description: Original signed Gemini sentiment score when the effective score was capped because grounding returned no sources.

sentiment_score_evidence.description: Model's justification naming the reference anchor band it scored against and the observation behind that choice (GH-1031). Present when the prompt returns one; bounded to 240 characters. Absent for prompts that predate the anchor rubric.

price_data.description: Optional structured TradingView MCP price snapshot (e.g. current_price, high, low).

setup_evidence.description: Optional one-line rationale or observed market structure supporting the setup_type

symbol.description: Symbol whose configured route produced this delivery result. Present when symbolRoutes is used.

alertId.description: Stored alert ID echoed back from replay endpoints.

channels.description: Channels selected for this replay; when dryRun is true, no dispatch occurs.

idempotencyKeyHashPrefix.description: SHA-256 hash prefix (12 characters) of the idempotency key echoed back from replay endpoints to identify the request without exposing the raw key in cached responses.

payloadPreview.description: Returned only by replay endpoints when dryRun=true. Contains the exact payload that would be dispatched (text, enriched data, channel routing) without sending to any channel or persisting a replay attempt.

enriched.description: Stored enrichmentData from the alert. Mirrors the alert.enriched shape (may include sentiment, insights, technical_levels, etc.).

channelRouting.description: Per-channel effective destination routing that would have been applied (telegramChatId, telegramThreadId, whatsappChatId, discordWebhookUrl), resolving channel service defaults and topic routes when stored alert lacks overrides.

replayId.description: Persisted replay attempt ID returned only on live replay; absent when dryRun=true.

WebhookAlertDeliveryResult.description: Response for POST /api/webhook/alert. Mirrors the shared DeliveryResult schema and adds endpoint-specific truncation metadata: when the shared alert validator clips submitted text above 4,000 characters the response carries truncated: true, originalLength, and deliveredLength. All three are absent when the text fits, and they never appear on alert replay responses.

truncated.description: True when the shared alert validator clipped submitted text above 4,000 characters.

originalLength.description: Character length of the alert text as submitted, before truncation.

deliveredLength.description: Character length of the alert text actually processed and delivered, including the appended ellipsis.

idempotencyReplayed.description: Present and true when the response was replayed from a matching idempotency key.

status.description: Current job status. Terminal statuses are: completed, failed, cancelled, timed_out.

callbackStatus.description: Callback delivery state, present only when a callbackUrl was configured.

results.description: Per-symbol analysis results (expanded-analysis jobs only, when completed).

scanResults.description: Per-scan results (market-scanner jobs only, when completed). Ranked jobs include scores with symbol, score, reason, and optional trendConfluence entries.

alertText.description: Formatted alert text delivered to notification channels (completed jobs only).

error.description: Error message (failed or timed_out jobs only).

code.description: Machine-readable error code (failed or timed_out jobs only).

symbol.description: Allow-listed Binance Spot symbol, for example BTCUSDT.

quantity.description: Base-asset quantity. Required for LIMIT. Optional for MARKET (evaluated using average price against the notional cap; MARKET BUYs are converted to an exchange-enforced quoteOrderQty at the estimated average price). Send as a string when exact decimal precision matters.

quoteOrderQty.description: Quote-asset amount for MARKET orders. Send as a string when exact decimal precision matters.

price.description: Required for LIMIT orders. Send as a string when exact decimal precision matters.

timeInForce.description: LIMIT-only. MARKET orders must omit this field.

clientOrderId.description: Stable Binance order identity. Required for live requests unless an idempotency key is supplied.

dryRun.description: Validate filters and notional without submitting. Set false only for an enabled operator workflow.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional body form of the idempotency key. Header form is preferred and required for live requests without clientOrderId.

idempotency_key.description: Optional snake_case body form of the idempotency key.

BinanceOrderPreviewRequest.description: Pre-trade preview body. The endpoint never calls submitNewOrder; the response includes a 5-second expiresAt token. maxSlippageBps is honored for MARKET BUY orders that include a depth snapshot.

symbol.description: Allow-listed Binance Spot symbol, for example BTCUSDT.

quantity.description: Base-asset quantity. Required for LIMIT. Optional for MARKET (must be paired with quoteOrderQty when provided).

timeInForce.description: LIMIT-only. MARKET orders must omit this field.

maxSlippageBps.description: Optional slippage budget in basis points. MARKET BUY orders with an available depth snapshot return wouldExceedBudget when the slippageBps estimate exceeds this value; the budget never rejects the preview itself.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which the preview must not be replayed.

previewFingerprint.description: Short SHA-256 fingerprint of the preview parameters and expiry.

TradingViewMcpRuntimeStatus.description: Fail-open TradingView MCP runtime telemetry. Terminal provider outages are classified as provider_unavailable and do not consume same-operation retries; provider response bodies and URLs are never exposed.

enrichment.description: Alert-path enrichment telemetry. `alertPath` aggregates the whole webhook enrichment path (full/partial/failed), so it cannot attribute an outcome to the confluence call specifically; `confluence` reports the optional ENABLE_TRADINGVIEW_CONFLUENCE_ENRICHMENT calls on their own (issue #1109). Counters are process-local and reset on restart.

confluence.description: Confluence enrichment counters, measured in CALLS rather than alerts: one alert enrichment issues up to two confluence calls (`combined_analysis`, then `multi_timeframe_analysis` when multi-timeframe mode is enabled). Each issued call records exactly one outcome, so `appliedCount + failedCount <= attemptedCount`. `budgetExhaustedCount` counts stages skipped because the enrichment budget was already spent, which is not a call. `enabled: true` with every counter at 0 means the gate is on but no alert has exercised it yet.

attemptedCount.description: Confluence calls issued. One alert enrichment contributes up to two: one `combined_analysis`, plus one `multi_timeframe_analysis` when multi-timeframe mode is enabled.

appliedCount.description: Confluence calls that returned data and were applied to the alert.

failedCount.description: Confluence calls that failed. Fail-open: a failure never blocks alert delivery. Because each issued call records exactly one outcome, `appliedCount + failedCount` never exceeds `attemptedCount`.

budgetExhaustedCount.description: Confluence stages skipped because the enrichment budget was already spent, so no call was issued at that stage. Not a call, and therefore not part of `attemptedCount`.

lastAppliedAt.description: Timestamp of the last confluence result applied to an alert, or null.

lastFailureCategory.description: Closed-enum category of the last confluence failure, or null. Provider response bodies and error messages are never exposed.

FirebaseRemoteConfigDependency.description: Safe runtime metadata for Firebase Remote Config server-side template loader without returning remote parameter values or secrets.

enabled.description: Whether Firebase Remote Config is enabled via ENABLE_FIREBASE_REMOTE_CONFIG.

ready.description: True only after a successful, fresh server template load; false if uninitialized, disabled, misconfigured, failed, or stale. `enabled` and `configured` being true does NOT imply readiness.

templatePublished.description: True only when the `firebase-server` namespace template has been fetched successfully at least once. Distinguishes 'wired up' (enabled + configured) from 'actually serving remote values' (issue #598).

status.description: Granular lifecycle state of the server template loader.

templateVersion.description: Version number of the currently loaded Remote Config template, or null.

lastSuccessfulLoad.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent successful template load, or null.

lastErrorCategory.description: Sanitized error category if the last load failed, returned values are stale, or a successful load produced values that failed schema validation (`invalid_value`), or null. `template_not_published` means the `firebase-server` namespace has no template yet and must be published (see the deploy:firebase-remote-config:server workflow); it is distinct from a transient `load_failed`.

consecutiveFailures.description: Count of consecutive failed template loads since last success; reset to 0 on success.

refreshIntervalMs.description: Configured background refresh interval in milliseconds.

maxAgeMs.description: Configured cache max age in milliseconds before values are considered stale.

NotificationChannelIntent.description: Operator-intent view of notification channel configuration, mirroring NotificationChannel.isConfigured(): a channel counts as configured when its enable flag is set AND its required credentials/chat id/webhook are present. A channel with credentials present but its enable flag off is therefore NOT configured, matching the verdict the zero-channel admin page reaches because both call the same method. This lets an operator answer 'why did I get the zero-channel page?' from the status response alone. Channel names only; no credentials or destinations are exposed.

configured.description: Channel names the operator configured, regardless of runtime readiness.

unconfigured.description: Channel names the operator never configured (missing credentials, webhook URL, or chat id).

AdminPagingStatus.description: Non-secret health of the operator paging path. Channel readiness blocks report 'ready' from configuration alone, so they report ready for a channel that is failing 100% of live sends. This block reports whether operator pages are actually landing, and which channels can carry a page when the primary Telegram admin destination cannot. Channel names, counters, and a truncated error string only; never tokens, webhook URLs, or chat ids. Omitted entirely when no NotificationManager has been constructed.

enabled.description: Whether an admin destination is configured at all (TELEGRAM_ADMIN_NOTIFICATIONS_CHAT_ID, or a usable fallback channel).

status.description: unknown before the first page attempt, ready once at least one page landed, degraded when every attempted page failed on every operator channel.

telegramAdminChatConfigured.description: Whether the primary Telegram admin chat id is configured.

fallbackEnabled.description: Whether at least one alternate operator channel is configured and eligible to carry a page.

fallbackChannels.description: Alternate channel names eligible to carry a page, ordered by observed delivery health. Only channels the operator configured are listed, so a never-configured channel never produces a phantom page.

attempts.description: Total per-channel admin page attempts in this process.

successes.description: Admin page attempts that were delivered.

consecutiveFailures.description: Admin page attempts failed since the last successful page. This is the signal external uptime monitoring can page on.

lastError.description: Truncated last admin page error, sanitized. Never contains a token, webhook URL, or chat id.

TelegramCommandAuthStatus.description: Safe runtime metadata for the Telegram command allowlist gate. Reports no chat ids; deniedSender counts only.

enabled.description: True when at least one chat id is authorized.

allowlistSource.description: Which variable supplied the allowlist; falls back to TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID when the explicit list is unset.

deniedSinceStart.description: Lifetime count of denied commands that produced a log line; cooldown-suppressed repeats are not counted.

trackedDeniedSenders.description: Chat ids currently held in the bounded log-cooldown cache.

deniedSenderCacheLimit.description: Maximum entries retained in the cooldown cache; oldest entries are evicted first.

NotificationRedriveDependency.description: Safe runtime metadata for dead-letter notification redrive worker without credentials.

enabled.description: Whether dead-letter redrive background evaluation is enabled via ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_REDRIVE.

configured.description: Whether redrive configuration is syntactically valid.

ready.description: True when redrive is enabled and role is not disabled.

status.description: Operational readiness state of notification redrive.

role.description: Effective worker role (web, worker, or disabled).

running.description: Whether the background redrive evaluation loop is running in the current process.

intervalMs.description: Configured redrive sweep interval in milliseconds.

batchLimit.description: Maximum number of dead-letter records evaluated per sweep.

maxAttempts.description: Maximum delivery attempts before a dead-letter record is marked exhausted.

maxAgeMs.description: Maximum age of a dead-letter record in milliseconds before expiration.

pendingCount.description: Current number of dead letters awaiting redrive delivery.

deliveredCount.description: Cumulative total number of successfully redriven dead-letter deliveries.

exhaustedCount.description: Cumulative total number of dead-letter records that reached max attempts or expired.

zeroChannelBroadcasts.description: Cumulative count of broadcast alerts dropped because no notification channels were enabled at broadcast time.

lastRunAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the redrive worker last initiated a sweep, or null.

lastSweepAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the redrive worker last completed a sweep, or null.

lastRunDurationMs.description: Duration of the last completed redrive sweep in milliseconds, or null.

lastRunScannedCount.description: Number of dead-letter records scanned in the last completed sweep.

lastRunRedrivenCount.description: Number of dead-letter records successfully redriven in the last completed sweep.

lastRunErrorCount.description: Number of delivery errors encountered in the last completed sweep.

lastRunExhaustedCount.description: Number of dead-letter records marked exhausted or expired in the last completed sweep.

lastSweepResult.description: Structured summary metrics of the last completed redrive sweep, or null if no sweep has completed.

exhausted.description: Total records marked exhausted or expired during the sweep.

errors.description: Total delivery errors encountered during the sweep.

NewsMonitorCacheSize.description: Safe operational counters and capacity bounds for the in-memory news monitor deduplication cache and URL shortener.

entries.description: Current number of in-memory news cache entries.

maxEntries.description: Maximum capacity of the in-memory news cache.

evictionCount.description: Total number of LRU cache entries evicted since startup.

deliveryLocks.description: Current number of in-memory delivery lock leases.

deliveryLockMaxEntries.description: Maximum capacity of the in-memory delivery lock map.

deliveryLockEvictionCount.description: Total number of delivery lock entries evicted since startup.

NewsMonitorDedupDependency.description: Safe runtime metadata for news monitor deduplication and cache size bounds without exposing sensitive credentials.

enabled.description: Whether persistent news deduplication is enabled via ENABLE_NEWS_MONITOR_PERSISTENT_DEDUP.

configured.description: Whether Firestore is configured for persistent news deduplication.

ready.description: True when persistent deduplication is ready and connected to Firestore.

status.description: Operational readiness status (ready, disabled, degraded, misconfigured).

backend.description: Storage backend provider name (e.g. firestore) or null if running in-memory.

TokenCostBudgetDependency.description: Safe runtime metadata for aggregate daily token spend tracking and budget alerting ceiling without exposing sensitive keys.

enabled.description: Whether daily token cost budget tracking and threshold alerting are enabled.

configured.description: Whether token cost budget tracking is configured.

ready.description: Whether token cost budget is ready and below the daily hard ceiling.

status.description: Operational budget state: disabled when feature is off, ready when spend is normal, warning when above alert threshold, exceeded when hard limit reached.

dailySpendUsd.description: Aggregate daily token spend in USD for the current UTC calendar day.

budgetUsd.description: Daily token cost budget ceiling in USD.

utilizationPct.description: Current percentage of daily budget utilized.

alertsSent.description: Number of budget alert notifications dispatched during the current UTC day.

lastResetAt.description: ISO timestamp of the last daily spend rollover (00:00 UTC).

symbol.description: Allow-listed Binance Spot symbol, for example BTCUSDT.

orderId.description: Binance-assigned order ID returned by the original POST /api/trading/binance/orders response. Provide exactly one of orderId or origClientOrderId.

origClientOrderId.description: Stable client-side order ID originally submitted with the order. Provide exactly one of orderId or origClientOrderId.

falsePositiveProxy.description: False-positive proxy measured over DELIVERED alerts only. Analyses that never sent an alert are excluded, because the proxy tracks delivered-alert outcomes rather than raw analysis scores. A delivered alert is counted as a false positive when no subsequent delivered alert for the same symbol arrived within 24h.

threshold.description: Confidence threshold applied to delivered alerts. Defaults to 0.7.

totalEvaluated.description: Number of delivered alerts at or above the threshold with a non-`none` event category that were evaluated for a follow-up.

noFollowupCount.description: Evaluated delivered alerts that had no subsequent delivered alert for the same symbol within 24h.

ratePercent.description: `noFollowupCount / totalEvaluated` as a percentage, rounded to two decimals. Zero when nothing was evaluated.

reason.description: Optional operational reason for pausing news monitor analysis

JobExecutionQueueDependency.description: Async job execution queue readiness plus durable backlog depth. A bounded, fail-open broker readiness probe runs at web startup when JOB_EXECUTION_MODE=render-worker, so brokerReachable reflects proven connectivity rather than the mere presence of a broker URL; this is what lets an operator confirm a render-worker cut-over from /api/capabilities alone on an idle deployment. Reports bounded broker counts and non-terminal durable queued rows so an operator can tell a ready-but-undrained queue apart from a healthy one. No Redis URL, broker credential, or chat destination is ever exposed.

enabled.description: Whether a broker-backed queue is enabled for this process.

configured.description: Whether the queue transport is configured. This only validates that a broker URL is present; it is not evidence that the broker is reachable. Read brokerReachable for that.

ready.description: Whether the queue can currently accept work.

status.description: Coarse queue state. `misconfigured` means queue mode is enabled without a broker URL. `not_started` means the broker has not been probed yet, which is not evidence of health. `unreachable` means the startup readiness probe ran and the broker did not answer within the probe deadline. `ready` means a probe has proven broker connectivity.

queueName.description: BullMQ queue name. Never contains credentials.

brokerReachable.description: Result of the bounded broker readiness probe: true once a probe has proven connectivity, false when the last probe ran and the broker did not answer, and null when no probe has produced a verdict — which includes queue mode being disabled, a missing broker URL (misconfigured), and an enabled+configured queue whose probe has not settled yet. Unlike `configured`, this is evidence rather than configuration shape.

lastBrokerProbeAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent broker readiness probe, or null when no probe has run.

lastBrokerProbeErrorCode.description: Sanitized error code from the most recent failed broker readiness probe, or null after a successful probe. Never contains the broker URL.

lastErrorCode.description: Sanitized last queue error code, or null. Never contains credentials.

lastEnqueuedAt.description: When this process last enqueued a job, or null.

waitingCount.description: Broker jobs waiting to be processed.

delayedCount.description: Broker jobs in a delayed state.

failedCount.description: Broker jobs in a failed state.

durableQueuedCount.description: Non-terminal durable jobs in a queued state. Reported as a lower bound when the bounded probe truncates or rotates its scan, and null when the last sweep could not observe durable state.

durableProbeSucceeded.description: Whether the last sweep actually observed durable state. False means the durable depth is unknown rather than zero, so an unreadable backlog is not read as a drained one. Null before the first probe.

durableQueuedTruncated.description: True when the bounded durable scan reached its page cap, meaning durableQueuedCount is a lower bound and additional queued jobs may exist.

durableScanRotated.description: True when the durable scan resumed from a rotation cursor, so it covered only part of the collection and durableQueuedCount and oldestQueuedAgeMs are lower bounds.

durableCycleComplete.description: True when this sweep resumed from a cursor left by an earlier capped sweep and then reached the end of the collection, so the closing sweep and the windows it tiled with cover the whole collection. Recovery additionally requires every window in that cycle to be below the alert threshold, re-evaluated at the closing sweep's own clock.

oldestQueuedAgeMs.description: Age in milliseconds of the oldest queued job, or null when the backlog is empty or the probe failed.

backlogMonitorEnabled.description: Whether ENABLE_JOB_BACKLOG_MONITOR permits backlog probing. Null before the monitor reports. False means depth is not being observed.

backlogMonitorRunning.description: Whether this process has an active backlog probe timer.

backlogAlert.description: Operator paging state for the durable backlog. A failed probe never clears this latch, so a transient storage error cannot emit a false all-clear.

active.description: Whether a backlog alert is currently latched.

pagedAt.description: When the current alert was last paged, or null.

lastRecoveryAt.description: When the last all-clear was paged, or null.

ReadinessDependencyStatus.description: Per-dependency status block. Disabled dependencies are reported as `skipped: true`; failing dependencies include a sanitized `error` string and the per-dep latency.

ReadinessReport.description: Structured dependency validation report returned by `/ready` and `/healthcheck?depth=readiness`. Disabled features are reported as `skipped: true` and do not count toward the overall `ready` verdict. No environment variable changes are required to enable the probe.

ready.description: True when every considered (non-skipped) dependency reports `ready: true`.

latencyMs.description: Total wall-clock time spent running all probes in parallel.

status.description: Bootstrap status. Only present on the `/ready?depth=dependencies` variant.

components.description: Per-component bootstrap state. Only present on the `/ready?depth=dependencies` variant.

bootstrapReady.description: Bootstrap gate verdict, ANDed with the dependency verdict. Only present on the `/ready?depth=dependencies` variant.

LangfusePromptsDependency.description: Non-secret prompt-resolution telemetry that separates Langfuse CONFIGURATION readiness (dependencies.langfuse) from actual PROMPT SERVING. Configuration being ready says nothing about whether prompts are actually being served remotely, so a 100% local-fallback regression is reported here as servingStatus=local_fallback instead of looking healthy. Only counts, tiers, timestamps, per-prompt resolved source, and a closed error-category enum are returned; remote prompt content, prompt variables, and credential material are never included. Counters reset on process restart. Langfuse unavailability always fails open to the local fallback and never blocks alert delivery.

enabled.description: Whether Langfuse prompt management is enabled via ENABLE_LANGFUSE_PROMPTS.

configured.description: Whether LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY are both present.

ready.description: Configuration readiness only, identical to dependencies.langfuse.ready. It does NOT mean prompts are being served from Langfuse; read servingStatus and servingPrompts for that.

servingStatus.description: Actual prompt serving state. no_traffic means configured and reachable but nothing has been resolved yet, so serving is genuinely unknown rather than healthy. local_fallback means remote is enabled and reachable but every fetch has failed, so no prompt has ever been served from Langfuse. degraded means at least one resolution came from Langfuse and at least one fell back. unknown is the fail-open value used when telemetry itself is unavailable.

servingPrompts.description: True only when at least one prompt has actually been served from Langfuse in this process. This is the fact that makes a 100% local-fallback regression detectable.

label.description: Effective Langfuse prompt label, or null when prompt management is disabled.

cacheTtlSeconds.description: Effective SDK prompt cache TTL in seconds, or null when prompt management is disabled.

totalResolutions.description: Total prompt resolutions in this process, from either source.

localResolutions.description: Resolutions served from the local file-backed fallback.

localResolutionRatePercent.description: Percentage of resolutions served from the local fallback, or null when no resolution has been recorded. 100 means Langfuse served nothing.

remoteFetchAttempts.description: Remote prompt fetch attempts, including client-unavailable paths.

remoteFetchSuccessRatePercent.description: Remote prompt fetch success rate, or null when no attempt has been recorded. 0 means every fetch failed.

lastSuccessfulFetchAt.description: Timestamp of the last successful remote prompt fetch, or null if none has ever succeeded. Null is the direct signal that Langfuse has never served a prompt.

lastFailedFetchAt.description: Timestamp of the last failed remote prompt fetch, or null.

lastErrorCategory.description: Sanitized category of the last remote prompt failure, or null. Raw provider error text is never returned because it can embed request context or credential fragments.

consecutiveFailures.description: Consecutive remote prompt fetch failures; reset to 0 on the first success.

prompts.description: Per-prompt resolution counters, present only for prompts resolved in this process.

items.description: Per-registered-prompt resolution counters and last observed resolved source. Contains no prompt content, no prompt variables, and no key material.

name.description: Langfuse prompt name, for example alert-enrichment.

type.description: Registered prompt type: chat or text.

langfuseResolutions.description: Resolutions of this prompt served from Langfuse.

localResolutions.description: Resolutions of this prompt served from the local file-backed fallback in src/services/prompts/defaults/.

lastSource.description: Resolved source of the most recent resolution: langfuse, local, or null when never resolved.

lastLangfuseVersion.description: Version of the last Langfuse prompt actually served for this prompt, or null when the last resolution used the local fallback.

lastResolvedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent resolution for this prompt.

XRequestIdResponseHeader.description: Unique identifier assigned to the request. Echoes the inbound `x-request-id` when supplied. Set as a response header on every non-exempt route; handlers that build their own response body may also echo it as `requestId`. Absent on routes exempted through `REQUEST_DEADLINE_EXEMPT_PATHS`.
